observation_summary: The compiler fails to resolve typedefs when they are defined within a goog.scope using aliased names, leading to a 'JSC_TYPE_PARSE_ERROR' and node tree inequality.
reasoning_summary: The bug report states that the compiler fails to recursively resolve typedefs in specific scoping scenarios, despite being designed to do so for other names. This indicates an error in the implementation of the name resolution or type-checking algorithm, rather than a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a structural design omission (Function/Class/Object). The logic for traversing and resolving these names is flawed in its current procedural implementation.
evidence_used: bug_report_description: JSCompiler does not recursively resolve typedefs
failing_tests: JSC_TYPE_PARSE_ERROR. Bad type annotation. Unknown type b.c.MyType
failing_tests: Node tree inequality: STRING a.b.c.MyType vs STRING b.c.MyType
evidence_gaps: The specific file containing the faulty resolution logic is not provided in the snippets, only the test and traversal infrastructure.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves the relationship between aliased names and their original definitions, the root cause is the failure of the resolution algorithm to correctly traverse and map these names, which is a procedural/algorithmic failure.
The capability to resolve names exists; it is just failing to perform correctly in this specific context, which is an algorithmic defect rather than a missing feature.
